$comment: The experimental 32-class palette. Same shape as world/palette.json plus a group and a meaning per class, so the two can be compared directly. Generated by world/master/experiment/tools/writePalette.mjs.

classes.name: ocean
classes.meaning: Open sea. The base colour of the image: anywhere no land layer painted.

classes.name: shallow-sea
classes.meaning: Continental shelf, inside the 200 m isobath. Sea a ship can anchor in.

classes.name: lake
classes.meaning: Standing fresh water. Every lake down to 10 ha gets at least one pixel.

classes.name: river
classes.meaning: Running water. Every reach of Strahler order three and up, drawn one to three pixels wide by size.

classes.name: ice
classes.meaning: Permanent ice: ice caps, ice sheets, glaciers, shelf ice.

classes.name: polar-desert
classes.meaning: Bare frozen ground with almost nothing growing on it. High arctic gravel and rock.

classes.name: tundra
classes.meaning: Moss, lichen and dwarf shrub over permafrost. Treeless but alive.

classes.name: taiga
classes.meaning: Closed boreal conifer forest. Dark, dense, unbroken.

classes.name: taiga-open
classes.meaning: Thin boreal forest: lichen woodland, bog margins, trees with sky between them.

classes.name: conifer-forest
classes.meaning: Temperate needleleaf forest. Pine and spruce south of the taiga.

classes.name: broadleaf-forest
classes.meaning: Temperate deciduous forest. Oak, beech, birch.

classes.name: mixed-forest
classes.meaning: Temperate forest of both kinds together, which is most of northern Europe.

classes.name: rainforest
classes.meaning: Closed tropical moist broadleaf forest.

classes.name: dry-forest
classes.meaning: Tropical and subtropical dry forest, and open woodland with a grass floor.

classes.name: mangrove
classes.meaning: Salt-tolerant coastal forest standing in tidal water.

classes.name: swamp-forest
classes.meaning: Forest standing in fresh water: flooded forest, carr, varzea.

classes.name: steppe
classes.meaning: Dry temperate grassland. Prairie, pampas, the Eurasian steppe.

classes.name: meadow
classes.meaning: Moist grassland and pasture. Grass that is grazed rather than ploughed.

classes.name: savanna
classes.meaning: Tropical grassland with scattered trees.

classes.name: scrub
classes.meaning: Shrubland: maquis, garrigue, chaparral, xeric scrub. Waist-high and woody.

classes.name: heath
classes.meaning: Cool oceanic moor and heath. Heather, gorse, wind, no trees.

classes.name: farmland
classes.meaning: Ploughed and managed land, open field to the horizon.

classes.name: farmland-with-woods
classes.meaning: The mosaic: fields with woodlots, hedges and copses between them. Most of settled Europe is this.

classes.name: paddy
classes.meaning: Flooded cropland. Rice terraces and delta paddies.

classes.name: marsh
classes.meaning: Treeless freshwater wetland: reed bed, fen, sedge marsh.

classes.name: bog
classes.meaning: Peatland and mire. Acid, spongy, cold. The Swedish and Finnish mosse.

classes.name: floodplain
classes.meaning: Seasonally flooded grassland. Dry half the year, under water the other half.

classes.name: salt-flat
classes.meaning: Playa, salar, sabkha. Flat, white, and lethal to cross.

classes.name: desert-sand
classes.meaning: Sand desert. Dunes and erg, nothing growing at all.

classes.name: desert-stone
classes.meaning: Stony desert and sparse xeric ground: reg, hamada, gravel plain.

classes.name: alpine-meadow
classes.meaning: Montane grassland above the treeline but below the rock.

classes.name: bare-rock
classes.meaning: Scree, cliff and bare mountain stone.
